1.title: Performance Issues
1.text: Welcome to Module twenty-three: Performance Issues. It covers the exam area five point zero Network Troubleshooting. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. five point four Given a scenario, troubleshoot common performance issues: congestion and contention. Bottlenecking. Bandwidth and throughput capacity. Latency. Packet loss. Jitter. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: five point zero Network Troubleshooting (twenty-four percent). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Network plus N ten to nine exam objectives, version four point zero.

1.title: Wired performance terms
1.text: Wired performance terms. The figure shows this: Bandwidth, throughput, latency, jitter and packet loss on a path.

1.title: Wired performance terms, continued
1.text: Wired performance terms. Congestion or contention. Too much traffic for the link or many devices competing for the same resource; queues fill, packets drop. Bottleneck. The slowest point on the path that limits overall speed (a slow uplink, an oversubscribed switch). Bandwidth. The maximum capacity of a link. Throughput. The data actually delivered (always at or below the bandwidth). Latency. Delay: time for a packet to travel (ms); high with satellite, distance, congestion. Packet loss. Packets that never arrive; causes retransmissions and bad voice and video. Jitter. Variation in delay between packets; hurts voice and video (choppy audio). Exam tip: Choppy voice and video equals jitter, latency or packet loss. Fix with Qo S, more bandwidth, or removing the bottleneck. Bandwidth is capacity; throughput is what you actually get.

1.title: Common wired causes and fixes
1.text: Common wired causes and fixes. Saturated uplink. Upgrade the link, add link aggregation, apply Qo S. Duplex or speed mismatch. Match both ends (auto-negotiate). Broadcast storm or loop. S T P, remove the loop. Faulty cable or N I C. Replace; check counters. Oversubscription. Add capacity or redesign (for example spine and leaf).

1.title: Wireless performance issues
1.text: Wireless performance issues. Interference. Other radios (microwave, Bluetooth, neighbor A P s), non-Wi-Fi sources; move to five gigahertz or six gigahertz, use a spectrum analyzer. Channel overlap. Neighboring A P s on overlapping channels; use one, six and eleven at two point four gigahertz. Signal degradation or loss. Distance, walls, metal, water; move the A P, raise power, use better antennas. Insufficient coverage. Dead spots; add A P s after a site survey and heat map. Exam tip: Jitter and packet loss ruin voice and video; bandwidth is capacity, throughput is what you get.

1.title: Wireless performance issues, continued
1.text: Wireless performance issues. Client disassociation. Clients drop off the network: weak signal, too many clients, authentication or power-save problems, channel interference. Roaming misconfiguration. Clients cling to a distant A P or drop when moving; same S S I D, security and V L A N on all A P s, correct power and thresholds, fast roaming (eight oh two dot eleven R). Exam tip: "Wi-Fi is slow only in one corner" equals coverage or signal degradation; check the heat map. "Clients drop when walking between A P s" equals roaming configuration.

1.title: Wireless performance issues, continued
1.text: Wireless performance issues. Exam tip: Wireless: use channels one, six and eleven at two point four gigahertz; check the heat map for coverage gaps.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Voice calls are choppy because packet delay varies widely. Which term describes this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Jitter. Jitter is variation in delay.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A one gigabit per second link delivers only four hundred megabits per second of useful data. Which statement is correct? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Throughput is lower than the link bandwidth. Throughput is actual delivered data and is at most the bandwidth.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Two neighboring A P s on channels three and four cause slow Wi-Fi. What is the best fix? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Move them to non-overlapping channels such as one and six. Non-overlapping channels remove the interference.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Users walking between floors lose their video calls as they move between A P s. What should be reviewed? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Roaming configuration on the A P s and controller. Roaming misconfiguration drops clients between A P s.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. An upgraded branch is still slow because all traffic funnels through one one hundred megabits per second uplink. What is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A bottleneck. The slowest link limits overall speed.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Wi-Fi is weak only in one corner of the building. What is the best next step? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Review the wireless heat map and add or move an A P. A heat map reveals coverage gaps.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the difference between bandwidth and throughput? Answer: Bandwidth is capacity; throughput is the data actually delivered. Question two. What does latency measure? Answer: The delay a packet experiences traveling. Question three. What is a bottleneck? Answer: The slowest point that limits overall speed.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is client disassociation? Answer: A wireless client dropping off the network. Question five. Name two causes of wireless interference. Answer: For example neighboring A P s and microwave ovens. Question six. What helps voice quality on a congested link? Answer: Qo S prioritizing the voice traffic.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Terms: bandwidth (capacity), throughput (delivered), latency (delay), jitter (delay variation), packet loss. Wired: congestion, bottleneck, duplex mismatch, loops; Qo S, upgrades. Wireless: interference, channel overlap, signal loss, coverage, disassociation, roaming. Fixes: Qo S, channels one or six or eleven, five or six gigahertz, heat map and more A P s.
